forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

compliance.notes: Strong on the 2021-Code fundamentals: a full-debt-profile liability benchmark charted to 2070/71, reconciled CFR and capital expenditure indicators, a thorough MRP policy with VRP overpayment disclosure, and complete governance/adoption appendices with a named scrutiny committee and quarterly reporting. Weakest on the newer commercial-investment disclosures: the net commercial/service income ratio (PI-08) is cited but never quantified, there is no limit on principal invested beyond 364 days (PI-10), no monetary service/commercial investment limits (COM-09), and formal statements are missing for paras 51-53 compliance, sterling-only borrowing and audit-qualification flagging. Several indicator tables also carry stale year labels (maturity limits headed 2025/26; interest-rate exposures ending 2026/27).

gaps.evidence: s58640 p.3 para 9: the required net commercial/service income to net revenue stream indicator is cited as a Code requirement, but no ratio or figures are produced anywhere
s58640 p.48: non-specified/property-fund investment levels can only be increased with Council approval; no quantified GBP or % ceiling on principal invested beyond 364 days per year
s58640 p.4 para 10: quotes the duty to state compliance with Prudential Code para 51, but no explicit compliance statement referencing paras 51-53 is actually made
s58640 p.48: pooled-fund (property fund) levels capped at approved amounts, increases requiring full Council approval; no stated monetary limits on total service or commercial investment
s58640 p.46: quantified fixed/variable exposure limits for investments only; no portfolio-level risk indicator (e.g. weighted-average credit score or duration)

news_drafts.headline: Hastings Council reschedules £11m debt for £2.3m lifetime savings
news_drafts.lead: Hastings Council has identified £2.3 million in lifetime savings by refinancing six loans worth £11 million, the Full Council heard on Wednesday. The council will take advantage of early repayment discounts worth £5 million to reduce replacement funding to less than £6 million, generating annual savings of around £515,000 in the first two years. The Treasury Management Update reported an additional £2.9 million net present value benefit from the restructuring. The move is part of efforts to strengthen financial resilience ahead of Local Government Reorganisation in April 2028. The council's longer-term pooled fund investments, meanwhile, have declined by approximately £562,000 from their initial cost, though the funds continue to generate dividend income of nearly 5 per cent and 3 per cent respectively.

findings.headline: CCLA pooled fund investments have declined by approximately £562,000 from initial cost
findings.detail: The council's longer-term pooled investments held with CCLA show significant mark-to-market depreciation. The Property Fund is now worth £1.788 million, down 10.60% from £2.0 million invested. The Better World Cautious Fund is worth £2.649 million, down 11.69% from £3.0 million invested. Though funds continue generating dividend income (4.71% and 2.87% yields), the unrealised losses reduce balance sheet asset values.
findings.matters: Deterioration in investment asset values reduces financial resilience and reflects market stress in the council's longer-term portfolio; material if forced to liquidate
findings.figures: Property Fund: £211,920 loss (10.60% of £2.0m); Better World Cautious Fund: £350,533 loss (11.69% of £3.0m); total unrealised loss ~£562,000
findings.quote: The value of the Property Fund as 30 June 2026 was £1,788,079. This is £211,920 (10.60%) below the initial investment amount of £2,000,000.

findings.headline: Council identified £2.3 million lifetime savings through rescheduling six PWLB loans worth £11 million
findings.detail: Six existing PWLB loans totalling £11.0 million at 2.484% average coupon can be refinanced by taking a 5.57% early repayment discount of £5.048 million. Less than £6 million replacement funding extinguishes the £11 million debt. The restructuring generates £2.311 million lifetime cash savings and £2.862 million NPV benefit, with £515,000 annual savings in years 1 and 2. The proposal strengthens financial resilience ahead of Local Government Reorganisation in April 2028.
findings.matters: Material financial improvement in the council's position during a period of budget pressures and immediately before merger into a unitary authority, showing proactive debt management
findings.figures: £11.0m outstanding debt; 2.484% average coupon; £5.048m early repayment discount; <£6.0m replacement funding; £2.311m lifetime savings; £2.862m NPV benefit; ~£515k annual savings years 1–2
findings.quote: The Council has identified an opportunity to reschedule six loans totalling £11.0 million, taking advantage of favourable market conditions and a £5.048 million early repayment discount to reduce replacement funding to less than £6.0 million. The proposal is expected to generate lifetime savings of £2.311 million and an NPV benefit of £2.862 million

findings.headline: All assets and borrowing liabilities transferring to East Sussex unitary authority from 1 April 2028
findings.detail: Six East Sussex councils including Hastings will be replaced by single unitary authority from 1 April 2028. Government proposals indicate all assets, liabilities, reserves, borrowing and treasury obligations will transfer to successor authority. Final structure and implementation arrangements currently being finalised. Proposed debt rescheduling positioned to improve financial position transferred to new authority, with benefit of front-loaded savings (£515k per annum years 1-2) realised during transition period.
findings.matters: Structural change creates fixed 19-month window for financial optimisation; lenders must understand council will cease to exist and all borrowing obligations transfer; timing of refinancing opportunity specifically aligned to strengthen inherited position.
findings.figures: 1 April 2028 vesting date for unitary authority
findings.quote: Under current Government proposals, the existing six East Sussex councils are expected to be replaced by a new unitary authority from 1 April 2028. Whilst the final structure and implementation arrangements are currently being finalised, it is anticipated that all assets, liabilities, reserves, borrowing, and treasury management obligations will transfer to the successor authority.

findings.headline: CCLA property investments marked down 10.6% and 11.7% respectively
findings.detail: Council holds longer-term strategic investments with CCLA: Property Fund valued at £1.788m (down from £2m initial investment) and Better World Cautious Fund at £2.649m (down from £3m initial investment). Total unrealised loss approximately £562k. Properties continue to generate dividend yields of 4.71% and 2.87% respectively. Losses reflect market valuations as at 30 June 2026.
findings.matters: Material reduction in strategic investment reserves available for deployment; identifies cash buffer weaker than headline figures; however positive ongoing yields suggest assets continue income-generating function despite losses.
findings.figures: Property Fund: £2,000,000 initial → £1,788,079 current (loss £211,920 or 10.60%), Better World Cautious Fund: £3,000,000 initial → £2,649,446 current (loss £350,533 or 11.69%), dividend yields 4.71% and 2.87%
findings.quote: The value of the Property Fund as 30 June 2026 was £1,788,079. This is £211,920 (10.60%) below the initial investment amount of £2,000,000. The value of the Better World Cautious Fund as 30 June 2026 was £2,649,446. This is £350,533 (11.69%) below the initial investment amount of £3,000,000.

findings.headline: Council anticipates £15.9m external borrowing requirement for 2026/27 capital programme
findings.detail: Q1 report forecasts borrowing of £15.9m will be required during financial year to fund capital programme expenditure. Actual requirement depends on capital programme progress, capital receipts from asset sales, and availability of cash balances for internal borrowing. Current external debt stands at £62.2m from 20 PWLB loans. Borrowing to be undertaken at 'most advantageous time' having regard to market conditions.
findings.matters: Material quantum of new borrowing signals significant capital investment plans; quantum relative to existing £62.2m debt base and £135m authorised limit shows headroom, but signals ongoing reliance on external funding.
findings.figures: £15.9 million anticipated borrowing, £62.2 million existing external debt, £135 million authorised borrowing limit, 20 existing PWLB loans at average rate 2.82%
findings.quote: It is anticipated that borrowing of £15.9m will be required this financial year to fund expenditure on the capital programme. This figure is however dependant on progress made on the capital programme, any capital receipts received within the year from asset sales and the availability of cashflows and reserve balances to facilitate internal borrowing.
